texts.preamble: Radha vs Sanjay on 11 August, 2025 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Ind:21548 1 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Indore Before Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pavan Kumar Dwivedi On The 11 th Of August, 2025 Misc. Appeal No. 9428 of 2024 Radha And Others Versus Sanjay And Others Appearance: Shri Chetan Joshi - Advocate for the appellants. Shri Sudarshan Pandit, learned counsel for the respon Order
texts.facts: 2. This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellants / claimants being aggrieved by the award dated 7/2/2024 passed in MACC No.10/2023 by the IVth Addl. Member, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Khargone, District West Neemar whereby a total sum of Rs.13,33,150/- has been awarded to the appellants / claimants by way of compensation. 3. As per the appellants, on 31/10/2022 Ajay Bavne (the deceased) was standing near the grocery shop of Idris and was talking with him. At that time respondent No.1 rashly and negligently came with motorcycle bearing registration No. M.P. 46 MW 7024 from Balakvada-Singun side and hit the same to deceased Ajay, as a result of which he suffered grievous injuries. He was admitted in the hospital, but eventually died during treatment. 4. Thereafter the appellants filed an application under Section 166 of the M.V. NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:21548 2 MA-9428-2024 Act, 1988 for award of compensation to them on account of his death. The application was contested by respondent No.3 Insurance Co. by filing its written statement to the same. Upon evaluation of the evidence brought on record by the parties the claims tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.13,33,150/-.
texts.arguments: 5. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the claims tribunal after considering the evidence on record awarded an amount of Rs.11,08,800/- for loss of dependency and after awarding compensation in other heads total compensation of Rs.13,33,150/- was awarded. He further submits that the claims tribunal has wrongly assessed the income of the deceased. He submits that deceased Radha vs Sanjay on 11 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30030275/ 1 Ajay was operating hotel in the name and style of Manbhavan Hotel where he was selling Tea, Samosa and Kachori and was earning Rs.1000/- to Rs.1500/- per day. In order to prove this claim the appellant Radha deposed as AW.1 and has also produced in evidence Exhibit A/18 which is the Food Safety Supervisor Certificate of competence so as to establish that Late Ajay was operating the hotel and earning Rs.1000/- to Rs.1500/- per day. He submits that there was no reason for the claims tribunal to disbelieve the income of the deceased when A/18 certificate was produced and statement of AW.1 has remained firmed in cross examination also. As regards the compensation in other heads he submits that even in other heads inadequate compensation has been awarded. 6. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Co. submits that the claims tribunal has correctly disbelieved the claim of the income of the deceased. He refers to the cross examination of AW.1 Radha particularly para 13 of her cross examination in which she has admitted that she has not brought the certificate of establishment of shop, the certificate from the concerned Panchayat the accounts and documents regarding the name of the hotel or even the photographs of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:21548 3 MA-9428-2024 hotel. Thus he submits that there was a clear admission in the cross examination that she has not brought any material in support of her claim regarding hotel business of Late Ajay. He thus submits that there is no material at all to believe the income of the deceased and for this reason he submits that the claims tribunal has rightly taken the income of the deceased on notional basis by treating him as unskilled labourer. As regards the compensation in other heads, he supports the findings of the claims tribunal and submits that adequate compensation has been awarded by the tribunal. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Hans Raj V/s. Insurance
